newsitem.title: UK: Oil refinery profits pressured again by Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Oil refinery profits pressured again by Singapore.

text.p: Profit margins at the world's oil refineries mostly fell last week, extending the month-long downtrend.
The losses were led by a $1 a barrel drop in Singapore profits which sank back to their lowest levels since February, according to Reuters calculations using standard product yields.
Ironically, it was a huge surge in profit margins in Singapore to over $6 a barrel that dragged the rest of the world's profits higher from February to April this year.
A complex plant in Singapore now makes $2.92 a barrel which is below the $3.22 average during 1996 but well above lows of under $2 seen during much of last summer.
The losses reflect a profound weakness in gas oil in Asia which has been undermining profits since the middle of April.
The premium for gas oil above Dubai crude fell to $6.99 a barrel last Friday compared to a peak of nearly $11 in April and an average of $8.17 so far this year.
Gasoline and fuel also fell against crude oil prices.
In the West Rotterdam profit margins fell but managed a partial recover at the end of last week despite firming Brent prices.

Complex refineries are making $1.95 a barrel which is virtually the same as the $1.94 average made last year. Less sophisticated hydroskimming plants fell to just 72 cents a barrel but were well above the 39 cents posted last Thursday.
Mediterranean refinery profits fell about 50 cents a barrel while those on the U.S. Gulf Coast were broadly unchanged.
